story.title: DR Congo and M23 Rebels Establish Roadmap for Peace Talks
story.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo and the M23 rebels have reached an agreement on a roadmap for peace talks, following a history of conflict in the eastern region. This agreement aims to outline the next steps and timetable for negotiations under the Doha framework, which had previously stalled amid ongoing violence. The U.S. State Department acted as a mediator in this process.

explore_lenses.label: Why does a roadmap matter if fighting persists?
explore_lenses.title: It shifts talks toward implementation
explore_lenses.summary: The roadmap is significant because the November 2025 Doha Framework was not itself a final settlement: it left protocols and practical commitments to be negotiated. The new plan pairs those talks with a ceasefire-monitoring mechanism and an implementation-review body.

claims.text: The parties agreed on sequenced steps and timelines for negotiating the remaining protocols under the Doha Framework, which they signed on November 15, 2025.
They also agreed to establish a mechanism to review implementation of commitments and address obstacles, rather than relying only on future political talks.
The Doha framework envisaged issues including restoration of state authority, humanitarian access and refugee resettlement as subjects for further negotiation.

points: The parties agreed on sequenced steps and timelines for negotiating the remaining protocols under the Doha Framework, which they signed on November 15, 2025.

explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: The joint statement does not publish the roadmap’s detailed timetable, the unresolved protocols, or enforcement consequences if either side fails to carry them out.

explore_lenses.label: How did the process reach this point?
explore_lenses.title: Earlier commitments did not end the conflict
explore_lenses.summary: The roadmap follows a sequence of direct Doha talks and prior ceasefire commitments that had not fully translated into implementation on the ground. It is also one strand of a wider set of DRC-Rwanda, African Union and international diplomatic tracks.

claims.text: DRC and AFC/M23 representatives met in Switzerland from August 17 to 21, 2026, with Qatar, the United States, Togo as African Union mediator, Switzerland and the AU Commission, to assess progress and problems in the Doha process.

Qatar had hosted rounds of direct DRC-M23 talks since April 2025; reporting on the November framework said both sides continued to accuse the other of violating peace terms and that fighting had continued.

The African Union has argued that durable stability depends on coordination among the Doha, Washington and African-led processes, credible implementation of agreements, and respect for African leadership.

story_report.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo and AFC/M23 have set a roadmap to revive negotiations under the Doha Framework after meetings in Switzerland. The plan establishes sequenced steps and timelines for negotiating remaining protocols and creates a mechanism to review commitments and address obstacles. The agreement, reached with the involvement of the United States and other partners, provides a process for moving talks forward but does not disclose the specific obligations or timetable that will determine whether implementation succeeds.

sections.heading: Doha Framework Negotiations
sections.body: The parties said the roadmap covers the remaining protocols of the Doha Framework, which they signed on November 15, 2025. The framework envisages further negotiations on restoring state authority, humanitarian access and refugee resettlement. In addition to scheduling the next stages of talks, the new arrangement establishes a review mechanism intended to monitor commitments and deal with obstacles to implementation.

sections.heading: Switzerland Meeting and Earlier Disputes
sections.body: DRC and AFC/M23 representatives met in Switzerland from August 17 to 21, 2026, to assess progress and problems in the Doha process. Qatar, the United States, Togo in its role as African Union mediator, Switzerland and the AU Commission took part. Qatar had hosted direct talks since April 2025, but reporting on the November framework said both sides continued to accuse each other of violating peace terms while fighting continued. The African Union has said durable stability requires coordination among Doha, Washington and African-led processes, credible implementation and respect for African leadership.

unresolved.text: The joint statement does not publish the roadmap's detailed timetable, identify the remaining protocols, or specify enforcement consequences for noncompliance. Official accounts also do not say which earlier implementation disputes were settled in Switzerland and which remain contested.

related_stories.title: Landfill Collapse in Conakry Results in At Least 30 Fatalities
related_stories.summary: A landfill collapse in Conakry, Guinea, has resulted in at least 30 deaths and six injuries. The incident occurred after heavy rains, leading to the destruction of homes in the area. Emergency teams have initiated a search and rescue operation to find survivors among the debris.

related_stories.title: Wildfire Forces Evacuations in Reno, Nevada, as Homes Are Destroyed
related_stories.summary: A fast-moving wildfire in northwest Reno, Nevada, has prompted authorities to urge the evacuation of approximately 90,000 residents. The fire, which has destroyed homes and complicated firefighting efforts due to shifting winds, has also endangered first responders and civilians. Fire crews are struggling to control the blaze as it jumps over fire trucks and creates hazardous conditions.

related_stories.summary: Leah Stewart, a 34-year-old woman from Sydney, has publicly expressed her gratitude for the support she has received during her recovery from a shark attack in June. She suffered multiple bites to her arms and legs but feels she has been given a 'second chance at life.'
